analyst_view.overall: Arsenal top the table with 24 points and are the only side in the league with a 100% home record. They host promoted Hull, who are 11th but have gone eight games without a win in all competitions. Arsenal played Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Wednesday and are without Bukayo Saka (quad), Max Dowman (suspended) and possibly Ezri Konsa, who was substituted early in Prague. Hull lose Matt Crooks to a fifth-yellow ban on top of a long injury list.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals. Arsenal win at home but don't run up big scores: 14 goals in nine league games. With Saka out and legs tired after Prague, Arteta's side may be more about control than goals. Hull under Sergej Jakirovic have a joint-high five league draws and tend to keep games tight.

corners.text: The numbers say about 10 corners, most of them Arsenal's. Hull are likely to defend deep away at the league leaders, and Hull's injury list leaves them few ways to relieve pressure. That points to Arsenal pinning them back and forcing plenty of blocked crosses and set pieces.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, with most expected from Hull. Hull lose Matt Crooks, their experienced, tough-tackling midfielder who is suspended after his fifth booking. Oli McBurnie is one booking away from a ban. A one-sided game in which Arsenal keep the ball usually produces fewer flashpoints.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.5 shots, roughly 17 of them Arsenal's. Hull sitting deep fits a high Arsenal shot count. Missing Saka and possibly rotating after the Champions League pulls the other way, so the model's figure looks about right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.7 shots on target. Without Saka, Arsenal lose their main source of chances from the right. A packed Hull defence should block plenty of efforts, and Hull have rarely tested goalkeepers away from home.
